scope: Actions artifact ordering during encrypted-state restore

change.ordering_source: GitHub artifact created_at timestamps, parsed as timezone-aware ISO-8601 and normalized to UTC
change.behavior: Artifact IDs are treated as opaque. The checkpoint artifact must be present and unexpired. Restore holds on missing or malformed timestamps, duplicate artifact IDs, or equal timestamps across distinct artifacts. A distinct artifact created later than the checkpoint triggers orphan_state_artifact_requires_recovery. The pointed artifact is downloaded and authenticated by unseal before restore succeeds.
change.bootstrap: Unchanged; first-run bootstrap remains explicit and fail-closed.

cases_added: Legitimate checkpoint with lower artifact ID than an older artifact restores and authenticates the pointed artifact
Newer orphan with lower artifact ID is rejected by timestamp
Missing, malformed, and timezone-naive timestamps fail closed
Equal timestamps across artifacts fail closed
verification.network: No live GitHub calls were made; fixtures and mocks only.

limits: Restore requires GitHub to return valid created_at metadata for every retained private state artifact in the bounded listing.
Timestamp ties are treated as ambiguous even when they might be harmless; operator recovery is required.
This review does not verify the live Actions artifacts or checkpoint beyond the supplied run evidence.
